Subject: Amberwood priority lane & audit export gating request

Team — quick ask in advance of tomorrow's exec sync with Amberwood. They just moved from POC to a conditional commercial commit (signed LOI attached) and procurement expects a production checklist by EOW. Two blocker items from their security/compliance reviewers: (1) an auditable export of model request/response traces for the last 90 days (redacted PII ok) and (2) tenant-level routing so certain high-value workflows run on dedicated capacity.

What we're asking: can Product/Eng scope a prioritized ticket for a '90-day audit export' feature plus an isolate-routing shim for a single enterprise CID that would allow us to guarantee residency in a Dedicated lane? Amberwood is willing to commit to a 12-month reserved pool if we can get a targeted delivery window (they want pilot in 6 weeks).

Impact: $1.8M ARR commit on the table (deal id AMBER-2026-0921). If we can't promise a reasonable path, they will escalate to Vendor Procurement and push for an extended evaluation or look at a competitor.

Next steps I suggest: 
- Marissa: can you evaluate product scope and confirm if '90-day audit export' can be supported by existing telemetry exports, and whether isolation can be delivered as a config + routing policy?
- Ben/Soojin: ballpark engineering lead time / major blockers (KV cache semantics, retention, indexing).
- Priya: can you own a customer-facing mutual action plan doc and procurement checklist?

I attached the LOI and their SLA matrix so you have context. I can join a short triage tomorrow 10:30am PT.

Thanks — Rishi
--
Rishi Malhotra | Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Amberwood priority lane & audit export gating request

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the heads-up and congrats on the LOI. 

Quick initial notes after scanning the SLA matrix and LOI:
- "90-day audit export": we currently have per-request traces for 30 days in our observability pipeline; extending to 90 days is non-trivial because the trace payloads are sizeable and retention policies affect storage/Ops costs. We could implement a gated export (on-demand export bundle) that queries historical traces and packages redacted payloads — that would be a product feature scoped as 'audit-export-runner'.
- Tenant-level routing / residency: Product can add a routing policy flag (dedicated-route: true) that signals the smart-router to prefer dedicated capacity. Full hard isolation requires Dedicated config changes and possibly reserved pool tagging. We can prototype a routing shim that guarantees affinity but not strict hardware isolation.

For both asks I need eng cost and a recommended MVP. Ben — can you do a quick feasibility estimate for: (A) audit-export-runner (query + redact + export to S3/secure bucket) and (B) routing shim + tenant affinity within Dedicated rollout? Aim for 3 buckets: quick-risk (2w spike), minimal-MVP (4–6w), full-isolation (8–12w).

Priya — please start the mutual action plan doc in Drive and link it here when ready.

I won't be able to make 10:30 tomorrow; propose 11:00 PT for a 30-min triage.

—Marissa
Product Lead, Platform
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Amberwood priority lane & audit export gating request

High level feasibility from Eng's POV:

1) Audit-export-runner (90d)
- Quick-risk (2w): build a safe query that pulls traces from our observability store for a given account and time range, run a basic PII redaction (email/hash replacement), and dump a zip to a secure bucket. This is engineering-light but operationally risky under load; can be gated to manual runs (on-call trigger).
- MVP (4–6w): add pagination, rate-limits, automated redaction rules, signed export links, and an approval workflow for compliance. Requires changes to trace indexing for efficient lookups.
- Full (8–12w): indexed exports, automated retention lifecycle, and integration with customer KMS for encrypted archives.

2) Tenant routing shim / affinity
- Quick-risk (2w): routing flag that biases traffic to a tagged Dedicated pool. No strict affinity guarantees — best-effort.
- MVP (6–8w): affinity tokens + warm-pool seeding + monitoring hooks to surface evictions. Needs changes in autoscaling logic and admission control.
- Full (10–14w): strict hardware-level isolation with tenancy tags throughout the runtime stack and accounting for billing impacts.

Major blockers: trace indexing (storage + query perf) and Dedicated pool tagging across orchestration layers. Both have medium priority but could be accelerated with a small focused squad (2 FE, 2 BE, 1 infra) if Sales secures the ARR commit and we get signoff for a short-term engineering uplift.

I'll sketch a one-page tradeoff doc and ETA ranges by EOD. We should also define success criteria Amberwood wants for the pilot (throughput, latency SLOs, export search latency).

—Ben

Thanks everyone — short update from infra/ops perspective after a quick spike:
- We can do the Quick-risk audit export and routing flag as safe, low-effort pilots. Ops will require a runbook and a manual approval workflow for the first three exports.
- To meet the pilot timeline (Dec 4) we need a dedicated 3-week fast-track: 2 engineers from runtime, 1 infra, 1 product PM. This would accelerate MVP to ~3 weeks for the routing shim and 2 weeks for an export-runner (manual-run mode).
- Cost implications: temporary storage and S3 egress for export artifacts will be billed to the deal (need procurement sign-off).

Marissa/Ben — if leadership approves a small sprint allocation we can be in pilot on Dec 4 with manual export gating. If not, the realistic timeline is 6–8 weeks.

Asha/Tom — can you confirm procurement's willingness to accept manual-run exports for pilot and the budget for storage/ops uplift?

—Soojin
